selection: Real sides are the shipped report's Verdict (first_impression) and flagged Critical Misses from the November 5 live-judgment outputs, verbatim. Composed sides are written to isolate one decision; each item's key names which.

decisions.variance: Two production runs on the same resume. Which Critical Miss set is right, or is there no real difference? (decision 17)
decisions.what_leads: Does the structural problem a reviewer trips on first lead, or the line edit? (decision 6)
decisions.deliverable_exemption: On a first role, is the Critical Miss the named deliverable or the count? (decision 4)
decisions.employer_tier_recent: Does a current top-tier employer lift the band when its lines are vague, said out loud? (decision 5)
decisions.employer_tier_old: Does a top-tier employer four years back lift a thin current role? The brief says no. (decision 5, the bound)
decisions.count_padding: On a strong resume, one Critical Miss or three where two are small? (decisions 7 and 8)
decisions.count_beyond_three: Three Critical Misses or five, when five would each cost the interview? (decision 7)
decisions.honest_mismatch: When the mismatch is plain, does the Verdict say it first, then the fix? (decision 9, Matt said idk)
